title: Numbers Above 100
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the numbers and the year example were reconstructed from context and standard German.
objectives: I can say and write the hundreds from 100 to 900
I can say and write thousands, millions and billions
I can build numbers like 634 or 3.915 in German
I can say a year, e.g. 1990

expressions.en: I was born in nineteen ninety (written out).

grammar.title: Hundreds
grammar.body: Hundreds are easy: take the number and add **hundert**. The word *ein* in front of *hundert* is optional: *hundert* or *einhundert*. Everything is written as **one word**.

grammar.title: Thousands
grammar.body: Thousands work the same way: **(ein)tausend**, **zweitausend**, **dreitausend** … In German a number with five or more digits uses a **point** as the thousand separator, not a comma: *11.000* = **elftausend**, *12.000* = **zwölftausend**, *20.000* = **zwanzigtausend**. Even large numbers such as *100.000* (**hunderttausend**) or *800.000* (**achthunderttausend**) are written as one word.
grammar.ar: في الألمانية نكتب فاصل الآلاف بنقطة وليس بفاصلة: 11.000.

grammar.title: Million and Milliarde
grammar.body: *Million* and *Milliarde* are **feminine nouns**, so they are capitalised and written as a **separate word**. For more than one, add *-en* or *-n*: *eine Million*, *zwei Millionen*, *drei Millionen* … *eine Milliarde*, *zwei Milliarden*. In German *eine Milliarde* is 1.000.000.000 (a thousand million).

grammar.title: Combining numbers
grammar.body: Always say the numbers in the same order as you read them from left to right: first thousands, then hundreds, then the last two digits. The last two digits follow the rule you know from lesson 4: units first, then *und*, then the tens (*vierunddreißig*). Write everything as one word.

grammar.title: Years (das Jahr)
grammar.body: For years up to 1999 German speakers say the number in hundreds: **1990 = neunzehnhundertneunzig** (nineteen hundred ninety). From 2000 on you say it as a normal number: **2000 = zweitausend**. To say when you were born, use *Ich bin ... geboren*.

mistakes.why: Numbers up to 999.999 are written as one word.
German uses a point as the thousand separator.

pronunciation.tip: *zwei* starts with *ts*: 'tsvai'. Say *zweihundert* as one word: tsvai-hun-dert.
In *dreißig* the *ß* is a sharp s; *zwanzig* ends with a soft *ch* sound in standard German.

tip: Read long numbers from left to right and write each chunk into one word. Practise with phone numbers, prices and years.

summary: Hundreds: zweihundert, dreihundert … neunhundert (one word; ein- is optional for 100).
Thousands: (ein)tausend, zweitausend, elftausend; the thousand separator is a point.
Million and Milliarde are feminine nouns: eine Million, zwei Millionen; eine Milliarde, zwei Milliarden.
Read left to right: thousands, hundreds, then units + und + tens (sechshundertvierunddreißig).
Years up to 1999: neunzehnhundertneunzig; from 2000: zweitausend.
